clue.text: Capital fellows - in pairs as required

indicators.note: the letters are taken as required, in whatever order the job needs, not the order printed

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter as raw material

explanation.surface: Men from the capital have to go about in twos, as the rules demand.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'in pairs as required' read as an instruction to the fellows; it is the anagram material plus its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: People living in Paris, the French capital, are called Parisians; 'fellows' stands for those residents.

clue.text: A rod for fresh-water fish

blocks.note: first meaning: an old unit of length, five and a half yards, also called a pole
second meaning: a spiny-finned river and lake fish

explanation.surface: An angler's equipment recommendation for catching river fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a fishing rod; here it is the old measure of land length.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old surveying measure equal to a rod or pole and a common edible lake fish.

clue.text: Controlling mechanism raising gun on a mount

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something lifts it so it reads from the bottom upward

blocks.note: taken as written
a Luger is a German pistol
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A device that controls the elevation of an artillery piece set on a mounting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' acts on the gun together with 'a', since a down light reads upward; 'on' then just places the result above the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulator is a device that controls the speed, pressure or flow of a machine.

clue.text: American students appear more posh so dressed

indicators.note: dressing up changes the look, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: US college kids look smarter when they dress up like that.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a sophomore is a second-year student at high school or college.

clue.text: A piece of writing that's just the thing!

blocks.note: first meaning: an essay or report in a newspaper or magazine
second meaning: 'the very ...' is the exact item wanted

explanation.surface: Praise for an essay that turns out to be exactly what was needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a written piece in a periodical and, in the phrase 'the very article', exactly the item wanted.

clue.text: Bound by the boss

blocks.note: to bound is to leap or skip
per means by, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: Someone is tied down, or obliged, by their employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound by' reads as 'obliged by', but bound is a leap and by is a Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the captain of a ship or team, so informally anyone in charge.

clue.text: A little bit of spirit shown in honour

indicators.note: one item is shown placed inside another

blocks.note: Companion of the Bath, a British order of chivalry
rum is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Someone receiving an award shows a small amount of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests courage; it is the drink. CB, Companion of the Bath, is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a tiny fragment of bread, and figuratively any small scrap, such as a crumb of comfort.

clue.text: Being firm, kept half the fuel

indicators.note: only half of the word survives, the rest being dropped

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
taken as written before being cut

explanation.surface: A resolute stoker held back half the coal supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being firm' sounds like a description of resolve; firm is a company. Only the first two of the four letters of kept are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is the solid fuel left after coal is heated to drive off gases.

clue.text: Concert given in the sun - it encourages attendance

definitions.note: verb: to arrange or act together

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters straddle the words, from the second letter of the first to the first of the last
surface padding, completing the picture of a crowd drawn by sunshine

explanation.surface: An open-air concert in sunshine draws a bigger crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' looks like a musical event; it is the verb meaning to act together.
explanation.definitionFit: To concert is to arrange or bring together by agreement, so it means to join forces.

clue.text: Game to make music?

definitions.note: a bagatelle is a piece of music, so 'make music' means compose one

blocks.note: first meaning: a table game rolling balls into holes, a forerunner of pinball
second meaning: a short light piece, often for piano, like Beethoven's Für Elise

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the music is a specific short composition, not music in general.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a board game with balls and pins, and a short, light instrumental composition.

clue.text: Telephone pointlessly to organise things

indicators.note: a compass point is removed, here north

blocks.note: to ring up is to telephone

explanation.surface: Making a futile phone call to get things arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointlessly' seems to mean in vain; it removes the N, the compass point north.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig up is to set up or arrange something quickly from whatever is available.

clue.text: Flashy second

definitions.note: the answer here works as a noun, 'in a twinkling', so it matches 'second' used as a noun for a brief moment

blocks.note: first meaning: sparkling, glittering on and off
second meaning: a moment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flashy second' reads like a showy runner-up; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes stars glittering and, as a noun, a very brief instant of time.

clue.text: A safeguard for the daylight viewer

definitions.text: A safeguard for the daylight viewer

blocks.clueFragment: A safeguard for the daylight viewer
blocks.note: surface reading: some protection for anyone looking about in the daytime
setter's reading: the source of daylight is the sun, so this protects an observer of the sun

explanation.walkthrough: 'Daylight viewer' sounds like anyone out by day; it means a person looking at the sun itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A helioscope is a telescope fitted to let astronomers observe the sun without eye damage.

clue.text: Inspect and put back casual shirt

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from its end to its start

blocks.note: to put something down is to set it
a T-shirt is a casual shirt

explanation.surface: Someone checks a T-shirt and puts it back on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to examine or try it out to check its quality.

clue.text: Explain a pro taking in many a European aristocrat

indicators.note: something taking in another holds it inside itself

blocks.note: taken as written
pro means for, in favour of
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
a count is a continental nobleman

explanation.surface: Explaining how a professional came to host a crowd of continental nobles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' looks like a professional; it is the Latin for 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give the reason or explanation for it.

clue.text: Lasted longer than an officer in unusual situation

indicators.note: one item is placed inside another

blocks.note: outré means bizarre or unusual; 'situation' just pads the surface
WO is a warrant officer

explanation.surface: Someone outlasted a military officer who was in an odd predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: Outré is a French loan-word meaning eccentric or unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear is to last longer than something else, so the past tense means outlasted.

clue.text: Superior children unduly put out

blocks.note: over means above, higher than
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: Well-bred children are annoyed for no good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests annoyed; here it means issued, as of banknotes or shares.
explanation.definitionFit: To overissue is to release too many shares, notes or stamps, beyond what is authorised.

clue.text: 4 down presented in narrative form

indicators.note: the letters are laid out afresh, presented differently from before

blocks.note: the answer to 4 down

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written up as a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference leads to the answer at 4 down, which supplies all the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a detailed spoken or written account of events, a telling in sequence.

clue.text: Strain within the board may be detected

blocks.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging
a strain is a breed or race

explanation.surface: Tension inside the boardroom is likely to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' suggests stress; it is a breed or lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something traceable can be found or followed back to its source, so it is detectable.

clue.text: Down payment made, a hearing-aid can be sent

blocks.note: the ear is the organ that helps us hear
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing-aid' looks like the device; the ear itself is the aid to hearing.

clue.text: A writer taking a tour he himself arranged

indicators.note: something arranged is put in a new order, here by the writer himself

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An author goes on a trip he organised personally.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry David Thoreau was the American author of Walden.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoreau was a nineteenth-century American essayist and naturalist, famous for Walden.

clue.text: Create a beastly row and seem angry, so get a place to stay

blocks.note: a cow's noise is a beastly row
to rage is to show fury

explanation.surface: Kicking up a fuss and fuming to get a room for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place to stay' suggests lodging; a boat stays at a mooring.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorage is a place where a boat may be tied up and remain, a berth.

clue.text: Medico, a non-drinker, was first to be spotted

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A teetotal doctor was the first one noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as seen; it means blotched.
explanation.definitionFit: Mottled means marked with irregular blotches or patches of colour, as dappled skin is.

clue.text: Edge into church

blocks.note: in means into

explanation.surface: Someone sidles slowly through the church door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a direction of movement, but it simply supplies the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move forward slowly and carefully, a little at a time, as one edges.

clue.text: Not favouring certain offers made by the opposition

clue.text: Set about the French in unpleasant conditions

blocks.note: taken as written
le is French for the

clue.text: High lighting is torment for top players

explanation.walkthrough: 'High lighting' reads as stage lighting; it is a military flare fired high.
explanation.definitionFit: A star shell is an artillery shell that bursts high in the air to light up a battlefield.

clue.text: Lie concerning strength of character

blocks.note: a fib is a small lie
re means about

clue.text: Each single woman is on track

clue.text: Didn't feel enough would be basically supportive
